title: Local Agentic Theory For Mobile Games — Shafik Quoraishee & Joanne Song, The New York Times
talk_summary: The NYT speakers describe experimental on-device agentic systems for mobile games: a local agent loop (perceive/predict/decide/act) for Space Invaders, a constraint-satisfaction agent for Mini crosswords, and an accessibility agent that dynamically tunes UI dials (input tolerance, step granularity, layout resizing) against WCAG 2.2. The core engineering message is that agents must operate inside hard resource budgets (space, 16ms frame time, energy) managed via a soft/hard constraint graph.

takeaways.technique: Constraint graph with soft/hard budgets per resource
takeaways.what_they_do: They model agent execution against a constraint graph over space, time, and energy, applying soft constraints on one axis and hard penalties on another so the agent doesn't over-optimize a single resource at the cost of user experience.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're using like soft constraining on another area so that we're not penalizing too much if we need a little extra space but if we use too much time, we want to penalize that

takeaways.technique: Explicit perceive-predict-decide-act loop with visible agent state
takeaways.what_they_do: Their game agent runs a small fixed state machine (perceive scene, predict next threat, decide, act, loop) and surfaces those states in a UI so the loop is inspectable rather than a black box.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have a very few basic states where you're trying to perceive what's happening ... predict the next move ... deciding what to do next ... and then loop again

takeaways.technique: Budgeted compression of state history and planning artifacts
takeaways.what_they_do: They treat agent state history and planning artifacts as things that must be compressed to fit a fixed device budget alongside model weights and render headroom.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to compress the state history of the agent, you have to compress the working set or the planning artifacts of the agent

takeaways.what_they_do: Their crossword agent uses a satisfaction graph and backtracks when constraints get too crowded or incorrect, using natural-language graph state to guide the backtrack.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the constraints are getting too um uh too crowded or too incorrect, then it will backtrack efficiently

takeaways.technique: Honest benchmarking before shipping agent behavior
takeaways.what_they_do: They call for real benchmarks proving the agent actually improves outcomes, rather than assuming agentic behavior helps.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Faster chips paired with real benchmarks to prove that the agent makes things better.

takeaways.technique: Offload compute to local/edge to cut round-trip latency
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue for moving inference onto the device to avoid cloud round trips, framing latency and cost as the main drivers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you're not doing a round trip to the cloud to get that information. So you can actually compress that time
